introduction_markdown: This paper is arranged in two sections, A and B. Answer ALL questions in Sections A and B. Section A: answer ALL the questions (15 questions); the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: answer ALL four questions; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.

figures.legende: Figure 1: relation from P = {a, b, c, d} to Q = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}; arrows a to 2, b to 2, c to 4, d to 5.

incertitudes: Figure 1 (Q6) : la flèche de d se termine entre 4 et 5, nettement plus près de 5 ; lue comme d -> 5 (donc image {2, 4, 5}). Si elle visait 4, l'image serait {2, 4} et la liste des couples changerait.

questions.enonce_markdown: State whether this is a one - one, one - many or many - one relation.
questions.corrige_markdown:
From the arrow diagram: $a\to 2$, $b\to 2$, $c\to 4$, $d\to 5$.

Each element of $P$ has exactly one image, but the elements $a$ and $b$ share the same image $2$.

**It is a many - one relation.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Write down the Cartesian product $P\times Q$ of the sets $P$ and $Q$, for which the relation is true.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The relation is the set of ordered pairs read from the arrows (a subset of $P\times Q$):

$\{(a,2),\ (b,2),\ (c,4),\ (d,5)\}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: State the range of the relation. *[6 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The range is the set of images, i.e. the elements of $Q$ that are reached by an arrow:

**Range $=\{2,\ 4,\ 5\}$.** (The elements $1$ and $3$ are not images of anything.)
